event: A Sonoma County man who tortured his three adoptive children for years while collecting state adoption assistance benefits was sentenced Tuesday to life in prison without the possibility of parole, according to the Sonoma County District Attorney�s Office.Jose Centeno, 57, of Rohnert Park was found guilty by a July jury of three counts of kidnapping for financial gain, three counts of torture and nine counts involving the sexual abuse of a child. He was sentenced Tuesday to six consecutive sentences of life in prison without the possibility of parole, three consecutive life sentences, and an additional 39 years in the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation.In 2006, Jose and Gina Centeno adopted three siblings ages 2, 3 and 4 years old and enrolled them at John Reed Elementary School. In 2010, after a school staff member filed a report to Child Protective Services on suspicion of physical abuse, the Centenos pulled the children out of school and hid them in captivity.The Centenos told neighbors and extended family that the children had been given back to the state and were not living in their home. In reality, the Centenos confined the three children in an upstairs bedroom with a boarded-up window and chained them to their beds. At one point, the oldest sibling, Kaya, lost consciousness from the abuse. Her siblings were told that Kaya had been sent away, and they never saw or heard from her again. For years, one of the remaining siblings was not allowed to leave the upstairs bedroom except when Jose Centeno would take her to another room and sexually abuse her. In late 2018 or early 2019, Jose Centeno took the two younger siblings to live with family members in Mexico.All the while, the Centenos told state officials that the children were still in their care and received hundreds of dollars each month through the Adoption Assistance Program. They collected these benefits until their crimes were discovered in 2020.After the two younger siblings told people in Mexico about their abuse, Mexico CPS in July 2020 alerted Sonoma County CPS, kicking off a criminal investigation.Jose and Gina Centeno were arrested in August 2020. Gina Centeno was charged as well but died before the trial commenced. Sonoma County Superior Court Judge Troye Shaffer sentenced Jose Centeno to the maximum potential sentence for his charges. The oldest sibling, Kaya, still has not been found. Based on witness statements, she is believed to have disappeared in 2012, when she was 10 years old. �While appropriate that Mr. Centeno will be spending the rest of his life in prison, our two brave victims are still missing their sister Kaya,� said District Attorney Carla Rodriguez. �Though justice has absolutely been served in this case, Kaya will always be in our thoughts.�Anyone with information on Kaya�s whereabouts is asked to contact the Rohnert Park Department of Public Safety at 707-584-2630. Her missing person page can be found on the website of the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children.

event: Vending machines that dispense free naloxone, a nasal spray that can reverse the effects of opioid overdoses, have been installed throughout Marin County, public health officials announced Tuesday. Marin County now has eight naloxone vending machines and three Naloxboxes, wall-mounted boxes containing naloxone doses, according to an interactive map of naloxone distribution sites available online.�We�re excited to expand the availability of naloxone throughout the county,� said Dr. Todd Schirmer, director of behavioral health and recovery services for the county of Marin. �The new interactive map on the OD Free Marin website allows everyone to do their part by locating and carrying naloxone so they can be prepared for emergencies.�Though naloxone is available for purchase over the counter or by prescription, the new vending machines are an effort to expand access to people without insurance or who cannot afford the medication, officials said.�Vending machines are a great way to make sure everyone has access to Narcan in a no-questions asked, cost-free and equitable way,� said Dr. Matt Willis, Marin County public health officer, referring to a brand name for naloxone.OD Free Marin, a community-based overdose prevention coalition, will teach residents how to use naloxone to save a life at a Saturday event.Other Bay Area counties have also worked to make naloxone more available. event: Investments in fixed assets of the capital reached 6.8 trillion rubles last year, which is 3.8% more in comparable prices than in 2022, said the deputy head of the Department of Investment and Industrial Policy of the city Vladimir Petrakov.The statement was made at the session "Best Practices in Attracting Investments to BRICS Municipalities and Regions" at the VI International BRICS Municipal Forum in the capital at the Expocentre Central Exhibition Complex on August 27. About 68 billion rubles were invested in the implementation of the project. Thanks to this, more than 1.5 million residents of Moscow and the Moscow region have improved transport services. Offset contracts are also an effective form of partnership between government and business. Under the terms of the offset agreement, the business invests its own funds in the creation or modernization of production facilities for the production of products necessary for the city, and the capital undertakes obligations to purchase these products for many years.Thus, since 2017, the capital has signed 22 offset contracts in medicine, transport, microelectronics, and the food industry. The total purchase volume will amount to about 413 billion rubles. More than 7 thousand jobs will be created at new production facilities. Investors have already completed the creation of production facilities and started supplying goods under eight such contracts.In addition, the capital scales successful practices and concludes intersubject offset contracts. So, in 2024, Moscow concluded three interregional offset agreements: with the Republic of Karelia, Orenburg and Vladimir regions. Under the contracts, enterprises will be created to produce products necessary for landscaping and road construction.The city also provides investors with land for the construction of production facilities without bidding at a preferential rate of one ruble per year as part of large-scale investment projects (MaIP), and the use of the "green corridor" will help speed up administrative procedures and halve the construction period of industrial facilities. event: - Preserving the history of the city is an important part of the work of the Moscow government. Since 2011, we have been conducting it continuously and during this time we have already restored more than 2,000 monuments, including manors, temples, fountains, metro stations," Sergei Sobyanin said. - This year, about 50 cultural heritage sites have been restored to their original appearance, 150 more monuments are in line, work on which we plan to complete by the end of the year. In total, specialists are currently working on 500 objects.And here are just some of them.The earliest mention of these lands dates back to 1504. It is believed that their first owner was Fedor Voronets, from whom the Vorontsov boyar family descended.At various times, the territory belonged to the Grand Duke of Moscow Ivan III, then Ivan the Terrible, and under Tsar Alexei Mikhailovich they were given to Prince Boris Repin, with him and his descendants, a manor, outbuildings, a French park, etc. appeared.In 1812, the estate was rented by the former Moscow leader of the nobility Nikolai Obreskov in order to ... build a balloon here that could lift 50 people into the air at the same time. It was planned to be used at the Battle of Borodino, but something went wrong, and the work had to be curtailed.In Soviet times, there was a state farm on these lands, during the Great Patriotic War there was a line of defense of Moscow. This area became a park area only in the 80s. It is clear that its restoration is a long, painstaking and very expensive task.- We started the restoration of the Vorontsovo estate in 2019, - says the mayor of Moscow. - The southern service building, the eastern and western wings, two historical pillars at the entrance were put in order. The gate and the entrance bridge have been adapted for modern use. The rafters were put in order in the Gatehouses, dormer windows were replaced, facades of brick and white stone were cleared, doorways and white stone plinths were restored. A souvenir shop and an excursion service point will open there soon.The wooden mansion was built on a stone foundation, which remained from the building after the fire of 1812. The first owner was Baron Vladimir Shteingel, a participant in the Patriotic War of 1812, a Freemason who joined the Decembrists. Secret meetings were held in his house. Perhaps that's why they equipped a secret room behind the closet. It was accidentally found in the 70s of the twentieth century by restorers: they took hold of a beautiful mirrored door, and suddenly it went aside, opening a room decorated with decayed velvet with Masonic signs. According to rumors, the house also had a secret underground passage, but little is known about it.In the 70s of the XIX century, the family of the famous philosopher and psychologist Lev Lopatin settled here. His mansion attracted the most prominent people of that time: Leo Tolstoy, Ivan Bunin, Fyodor Tyutchev, Alexander Ostrovsky, Konstantin Stanislavsky and many others were happy to come to them on "Lopatinsky Wednesdays".After the revolution, the rooms became communal apartments, they were resettled only by the 70s. Today, the Department of Architecture of the Russian Academy of Arts is located here.The three-storey house was built in the XVIII century, it changed many owners. Among them were the parents of the future poet Fyodor Tyutchev.The building was damaged in a fire in 1812 and was sold to the city authorities. So the Myasnitskaya police station settled here, to which the fire department joined in 1825. Dmitry Kuvshinnikov, a doctor, lived at the police station with his wife, the artist Sofia. They opened their own literary and art salon, which was attended by Anton Chekhov and the artist Isaac Levitan. After the revolution, a police station was located here, and in the 30s - the Military Engineering Academy of the Red Army. Now it is the administrative building of the Higher School of Economics.The mansion was rebuilt many times, so reconstruction was not an easy task.:- Restorers replaced the building's utilities and restored the facade. Based on historical photographs, they replaced the street metal doors with wooden paneled ones, and plastic double-glazed windows with more authentic wooden windows," Sergei Sobyanin said. - Later partitions were dismantled inside, the pre-revolutionary parquet was restored. During the work, a small area with Metlakh floor tiles was found in the basement, presumably at the end of the XIX century. It was cleared and reassembled.ONLY NUMBERs50 monuments have been restored since the beginning of the yearWork on 150 buildings is planned to be completed by the end of 2024500 monuments are currently in operation

Something similar has already been created in the UK, the birthplace of the writer J. K. Rowling. And now the house has appeared in Russia.Correspondent MSK1.RU I went there and talked to the creator of the hotel.Hagrid's Hut itself (The Keeper's Hut) is located on a 15-acre plot about a 20-minute drive from Kashira station, far from country houses. When you drive up to it, it's hard not to notice the hut � it seems to be in the forest, behind the trees.Just outside the entrance to the courtyard there is a pointer to various places from the movies � arrows in the direction of Hogwarts, the Ministry of Magic, the hut itself, King's Cross Station, the Forbidden Forest, Diagon Alley, Hogsmeade and even Azkaban.The creator of the hotel, Daria Rahimi, invites me inside the house. She says that initially, when she and her husband Arsalan were going to build an ordinary house for rent here, she did not think that she would make a hotel for Harry Potter fans. The idea to create a hut did not come immediately: at first, Dasha became interested in a new hobby and began to assemble constructors based on "Harry Potter", and then her husband proposed to build a themed hotel.� My husband and I built the house at the end of 2023, and in February of this year we started renting it out. We did everything ourselves, because he is an architect-builder by education, I am a business manager, and also an amateur decorator," she says.The courtyard of the hotel now looks a little empty, so it is also planned to be filled. For example, put a bath tub for bathing in the yard and greenhouses.� It also needs to be equipped thematically, so that people can come and transplant a flower into a pot with a Mandrake written on it, some kind of appendage to remember themselves by, - said Daria.And there are many people who want to visit the hotel. There are practically no free dates for arrival until November, but New Year's are still free. You can book a hotel for two days or more � sometimes an exception is made and I book only for one. But, according to the creator of the hotel, guests often do not have enough time to enjoy a fairy tale.The cost of a night at the hotel is 12.5 thousand rubles on weekdays and 15.5 on weekends. On New Year's Eve, you will have to pay 50 thousand rubles per night.

event: Vadim Matyushin found an unusual stone on the territory of the former Chaika pioneer camp in the Krasnopakhorskoye settlement near Troitsk.
